globalRules: Write people, not systems. A line explains the world only if a person in the scene would say it.
Established lines are anchors, not a quota. Use each where the master places it; never repeat one to prove personality.
Black American and queer creative vocabulary belongs to specific people in specific rooms. It is never a quota, a seasoning or a joke.
Characters may interrupt, trail off and be wrong. Variation is protected: no character speaks in a single register all season.
Silence is dialogue. Grief, intimacy, confrontation and decisive choices default to performance, not narration.
Sloane's voice-over is selective, subjective and may be wrong. It never repeats what the camera shows.

characters.voiceIdentity: Warm, quick and expensive-sounding without trying. Bright on top, precise underneath. She sounds like the best guest at the party who also happens to be running it.

linguisticPersonality.vocabulary: Exact, visual, a little old-fashioned when she is being fond ("properly", "darling" only for objects and plants). Names people's staff and remembers details.
linguisticPersonality.phrasing: Short declaratives; verdicts in one word ("Brave."). Questions that are really invitations.
linguisticPersonality.humor: Self-deprecating about small things (ferns, directions), never about her judgment. Mischief and a little pettiness (dessert on someone else's tab).
linguisticPersonality.rhythm: Fast in public, slower and plainer in private. Jokes speed up when she is nervous.

relationshipLanguage.gideon-shaw: Sibling-like shorthand; lets him finish her sentences; argues for the fun of it; never flirtation.
relationshipLanguage.nadine-lockwood: Defensive charm first, honesty late. Season arc: learns to say "I need you" plainly (S1-61).
relationshipLanguage.richard-lockwood: Daughterly delight, performs competence for him; hears praise as proof of usefulness.
relationshipLanguage.kai-fontaine: Formal and careful after the exclusion; the old ease leaks through when they talk about making things.
relationshipLanguage.patrons: Asks more than she tells. From S1-52 her first question is "What do you want?"

emotionalPerformance.amused: Laughs with her whole face, then a dry one-liner.
emotionalPerformance.angry: Precise and quiet; sentences get shorter, never louder.
emotionalPerformance.grieving: Practical tasks and silence; voice-over withdraws.
emotionalPerformance.lying: Over-specific and charming; adds a detail nobody asked for.
emotionalPerformance.vulnerable: Plain words, no joke, looks away first.

establishedLines.line: If I can't dance in it, it's a costume.
I can get anyone into any room in this city. I can't keep a fern alive.
Every year I tell myself I'll stop deciding who gets what. Every year I'm very good at it.

characters.voiceIdentity: Low, unhurried, economical. Warmth arrives as dry understatement. Never raises his voice; does not need to.

linguisticPersonality.vocabulary: Plain words, precise nouns, no jargon or tactical talk in social rooms.
linguisticPersonality.phrasing: Statements, not threats. Corrections delivered as facts ("Your hair's perfect. Stop touching it.").
linguisticPersonality.humor: Deadpan; acts of care disguised as logistics (removing the cake plate).
linguisticPersonality.rhythm: Sparse. Lets a pause do the work.

relationshipLanguage.sloane-lockwood: Uncle-like intimacy; can interrupt without ceremony; respects her authority even while advising.
relationshipLanguage.richard-lockwood: Former protégé's affection; learning to dance from him.
relationshipLanguage.nadine-lockwood: Peer generation; frank, a little more formal than with Sloane.
relationshipLanguage.kai-fontaine: Firm and decent: the door is closed, the man is not insulted.

emotionalPerformance.amused: One raised eyebrow, a shorter sentence.
emotionalPerformance.grieving: Offers a handkerchief, not a speech (S1-49).
emotionalPerformance.lying: Rarely lies; declines to answer instead.

establishedLines.line: Car's downstairs. Your hair's perfect. Stop touching it.
There's a door for that, Royce. It isn't this one.
He can't ask. He has no standing. You know that.
Lead like you're not guarding the door.

characters.voiceIdentity: Articulate, charming and personable, with a dry, sarcastic edge he can switch off for direct sincerity. Founder direction of 2026-10-23 supersedes the hybrid's 'exuberant' register where they conflict.

linguisticPersonality.vocabulary: Maker's precision (materials, tolerances, light) next to the social fluency of Black queer creative rooms. Specific, never performed.
linguisticPersonality.phrasing: Well-built sentences; a setup and a dry turn. Writes better than he speaks when he is hurt (the note).
linguisticPersonality.humor: Sarcasm aimed up, never down. Self-aware about his exile.
linguisticPersonality.rhythm: Measured; speeds up only when he is explaining how something works.
avoid: Inferring or fixing his sexuality from styling or speech

relationshipLanguage.sloane-lockwood: Accountable, not grovelling. Old shorthand surfaces and is checked.
relationshipLanguage.celestine-rhodes: Son-like devotion expressed as argument about the work.
relationshipLanguage.gideon-shaw: Respect; does not test the boundary.
relationshipLanguage.neighbourhood-kids: Patient teacher; the warmest version of him.

emotionalPerformance.amused: A slow, private smile; one dry line.
emotionalPerformance.vulnerable: Says the true thing once, plainly, and does not repeat it.

establishedLines.line: Celestine has a vision she never built. She'll never ask. I'm asking.
